sentences.text: Shri Vinod Kumar Trivedi - Advocate for the appellant.

Ms. Ruby Haldkar - Advocate for the respondent No.1.
 Shri Ashok Shah - Advocate for the respondent No.3.
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 03.05.2018 passed in MACC.No.178/2014 by 1st Additional M.A.C.T., Jatara District- Tikamgarh seeking setting aside of impugned award/reduction of compensation amount.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to para 18 of the impugned award, submits that tribunal has wrongly determined respondent No.1/claimant's income as 9,000/- per month without any document on record.
Therefore, respondent No.1/claimant's income be determined on the basis of minimum wages.
On above ground, it is urged that compensation awarded by the tribunal be suitably reduced.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for claimant/respondents submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
No reduction is required.
Therefore, appeal filed by appellant is dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

6. So far as income of claimant/respondent No.1 Santram Asati is concerned, injured Santram Asati has deposed in his examination-in-chief that he used to run grocery shop and also used to sale and purchase grain (galla).

In para 16, the witness has deposed as under:-

g lgh gS fd firk gh enn dj nsrs gSaA vkosnd cSB ysrkA vkosnd FkksM+k cgqr MaMs ds lgkjs py ikrk gSA vkosnd dh eSa dksbZ enn~ ugha djrk gwaA ;
g dguk xyr gS fd vkosnu igys dh rjQ dke dj ysrk gS cSB ysr py ysrk gS vkSj igys dh rjg gh nqdkunkjh dj jgk gSA"
8. It is evident from above that applicant has not filed any documents pertaining to grocery shop/sale and purchase grain (galla).
It is also evident from above that the shop is still in existence.
Therefore, in view of above, in this courts' opinion tribunal has wrongly determined respondent No.1/claimant's monthly income as Rs. 9,000/-.
In view of facts and circumstances of the case, this court deems it appropriate to determine claimant's monthly income as Rs. 5,800/- per month.
Hence respondent/claimant's income is determined as Rs. 5,800/-. per months.

9. In view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
